heroText: Baghdad works best as a base in Iraq when you anchor days around Al-Mutanabbi Street, National Museum of Iraq and Al-Shaheed Monument. Use those sights to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Baghdad International handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Baghdad stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Baghdad hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.

history.text: The plan proposed to build a cultural hub on an island on the river, with an opera house, museums, a university, shopping malls, and a 300-foot statue of the fifth Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid.

Baghdad's early meteoric growth eventually slowed due to troubles within the Caliphate, including relocations of the capital to Samarra (during 808–819 and 836–892), the loss of the western and easternmost provinces, and periods of.
After Caliph Al-Amin's death in 813, the palace ceased to be the caliph's residence.
Another was established by Sabur ibn Ardashir in 991 or 993 for the literary men and scholars who frequented his academy.
In 1040, they destroyed the Ghaznavids, taking over their land and in 1055, Tughril Beg, the leader of the Seljuks, took over Baghdad.
The Mustansiriyya Madrasa, which owned an exceedingly rich library, was founded by al-Mustansir, the second last Abbasid caliph, who died in 1242.

Baghdad became a provincial capital controlled by the Mongol Jalayirid (1400–1411), Turkic Kara Koyunlu (1411–1469), Turkic Ak Koyunlu (1469–1508), and the Iranian Safavid (1508–1534) dynasties. Ottoman and Mamluks (16th–19th centuries) The Safavids took control.
In 1534, Baghdad was captured by the Ottoman Empire, becoming the administrative capital of Ottoman Iraq.
In 1921, under the Mandate of Mesopotamia, Baghdad became the capital of the British-protected monarchy.
